answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a whisper as the anchor of the cost.
